title: cross-company-operating-guides-2026
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data governance, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and reusable internal templates. It is intended as the single canonical reference for cross-functional teams and approvers.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and vendors with access to Redwood systems or who conduct business on Redwood’s behalf.
- Describes mandatory approval matrices, minimum technical controls, and operational workflows.
- Distinguishes low-risk day-to-day actions from high-risk production changes and vendor commitments.

Governance and ownership:
- Policy owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team).
- Day-to-day steward: IT & Security for access/data controls; Procurement for spend and vendor onboarding; People Ops for travel & expenses.
- Review cadence: annual review by owners; ad-hoc updates when legal/regulatory changes occur.

1) Access & Permissions (IAM)
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, enforce account hygiene, and provide repeatable provisioning/deprovisioning.
Key controls:
- Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Use standardized roles in the Identity Service (identity.redwood.internal). No permanent account should hold both Admin and Finance privileges.
- Provisioning flow (standard):
  1. Create Access Request using the Access Request template (link below).
  2. Manager approval required for non-admin roles. Security approval required for any IAM role granting write access to production namespaces.
  3. Provisioned by IT within SLA: 2 business days for non-prod, 4 hours for urgent prod if approved.
- MFA: Required for all interactive logins and CLI sessions; hardware 2FA is required for nominal admin roles.
- Account review: Quarterly access reviews; role owners must attest via the Access Attestation spreadsheet.

Example access request (YAML snippet):
```yaml
user: jane.doe@redwood.ai
request_reason: "Feature debugging - investigate latency regression in model-serving"
roles_requested:
  - svc-kv-readonly
  - dev-sandbox-writer
expiration: 2025-04-10
manager_approval: pending
security_approval: required
```

2) Change Management
All changes touching production systems follow the change process below. Non-production changes should follow lightweight review.
Change categories and approval thresholds:
- Standard change: Pre-approved, repeatable, documented maintenance (e.g., routine infra patching). CAB not required.
- Minor change: Low-risk config or code change; requires owner + SRE approval.
- Major change: Schema migrations, model rollouts, infra upgrades affecting >1 service; requires CAB approval and rollout plan.

Process (numbered steps):
1. Submit a Change Request (CR) using the CR template. Include rollback plan, test plan, blast radius, and monitoring playbook.
2. Owner and SRE review (48 hours). If Major, schedule for next CAB meeting (weekly).
3. Pre-production validation: run regression suite described in the CR and attach the logs.
4. Approve and schedule the window. Production change window: 02:00–04:00 UTC (default) unless business needs dictate otherwise.
5. Execution: one authorized executor only; notify #oncall and #incidents channels.
6. Post-change verification: run smoke checks and report using the post-change checklist within 2 hours.
7. If degraded, perform rollback steps defined in the CR and escalate per the incident playbook.

SLOs related to change process:
- Change approval SLA: 48 hours for Minor, 7 business days for Major (from submission to scheduled window).
- Post-change verification: 95% of changes must have green smoke checks within 2 hours.

3) Data Management and Classification
Classification labels:
- Restricted: Customer PII, payment data, export-controlled models. Encrypt at rest and in transit; access by exception only.
- Internal: Business operations data, internal dashboards. Encrypted at rest; access on need-to-know basis.
- Public: Documentation and marketing materials.

Retention and deletion:
- Customer PII: default retention 90 days unless contract specifies otherwise.
- Logs: short-term debug logs 30 days; aggregated observability metrics retained 13 months.
- Data deletion requests: follow the Data Deletion Request template and log to the governance tracker.

Backups and DR:
- Critical data (config, metadata, model artifacts) backed up daily with immutable snapshots; restore RTO target: 4 hours; RPO: 1 hour for critical objects.
- Annual restore rehearsals and quarterly partial restores for selected datasets.

Encryption and key management:
- Keys managed through Redwood KMS (kms.redwood.internal) or customer KMS for Private deployments. All production keys rotate at least every 12 months.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Approval matrix (high level):
- <$5,000: Manager approval.
- $5,000–$25,000: Manager + Finance approval.
- >$25,000: Manager + Finance + Legal review; Procurement team involvement required.
- Recurring subscriptions: treated like contracts and reviewed annually by Procurement.

Purchasing flow:
1. Submit Purchase Requisition with vendor, scope, and budget code.
2. Procurement evaluates vendor risk (SOC2, contracts) and creates PO.
3. Finance processes invoice on receipt and matches to PO.

Card and expense policies:
- Corporate p-cards: restricted to approved cardholders and limited to <$5k per transaction by default.
- Travel advances: require People Ops approval and reconciliation within 30 days.

5) Vendor Management and Onboarding
Minimum due diligence checklist:
- Confirm vendor legal entity and W9/W8 status.
- Security posture: ask for SOC2 Type II or equivalent; if not available, require risk assessment by Security.
- Contractual terms: data processing agreement, SLAs, data residency clauses if applicable.

Onboarding steps (simplified):
1. Business sponsor completes Vendor Intake form.
2. Procurement runs due diligence and assigns risk level (Low/Medium/High).
3. Legal negotiates contract terms; Security ensures technical controls are adequate.
4. Vendor is added to vendor registry with owner and renewal date.

Vendor performance and reviews:
- Quarterly reviews for strategic vendors; annual reviews for medium/high risk vendors.
- SLA targets documented in the vendor record; breach triggers escalation and remediation plan.

6) Travel Policy (business travel)
Booking and approvals:
- All trips must be pre-approved in Travel Request system with estimated cost and business justification.
- Use company-preferred vendors where available.

Per diem and reimbursement:
- Per diem standard rates mirror US GSA rates for domestic travel unless a negotiated vendor rate applies.
- Receipts required for any single expense >$75. Reimbursements submitted within 60 days.

Safety and incident reporting:
- If an employee is involved in an incident while traveling, notify People Ops immediately and file an Incident Report in the HR portal.

7) Standard Templates and Examples (links and text snippets)
- Access Request template: https://confluence.internal.redwood/access-requests (use the YAML example above as canonical).
- Change Request template: include intent, blast radius, rollback plan, and smoke tests.
- Vendor Intake template: fields for legal entity, contact, product, risk tier, SOC2 link.
- Expense report template: CSV and PDF forms available at Finance shared drive.

Example Change Request checklist (short):
- Title, owner, impacted services (e.g., model-serving-api, kv-store, config-service)
- Test plan attached (unit, integration, e2e)
- Rollback steps validated in staging
- Monitoring and alerts configured for the window
- Communications plan for customers and internal stakeholders

Escalation contacts and ownership (summary):
- Policy owner: Aisha Patel (Finance & Legal) — aisha.patel@redwood.ai
- Security lead (IAM & data): Miguel Alvarez — miguel.alvarez@redwood.ai
- Procurement lead: Sara Nguyen — sara.nguyen@redwood.ai
- IT operations (provisioning): Oncall primary channel #it-ops and email it-ops@redwood.ai

Appendix A — Definitions and abbreviations:
- RTO: Recovery Time Objective
- RPO: Recovery Point Objective
- CAB: Change Advisory Board
- SLA: Service Level Agreement

Appendix B — Revision history:
- 2025-03-10: Document created by Aisha Patel.
- 2025-08-05: Updated procurement approval thresholds (Procurement team).
- 2026-01-15: Clarified IAM provisioning SLAs and added YAML access example (Security).

How to use this doc:
- Teams should link to specific subsections in their runbooks and change requests. For any edge cases or exceptions, submit a Policy Exception Request to policy-exceptions@redwood.ai and include a compensating control plan.

End of document.
